the Government of India till December 2023?
questions.solution_text:
Delimitation Commissions in India are statutory bodies
constituted by the Government of India under the provisions of the Delimitation
Commission Act. The purpose of these commissions is to redraw the boundaries of
various assembly and Lok Sabha constituencies based on the latest census,
ensuring fair and equal representation given the demographic changes over time.
Here is a detailed breakdown of the Delimitation Commissions
constituted by the Government of India until December 2023:
First Delimitation Commission
: Constituted in 1952
after the enactment of the Delimitation Commission Act in 1952. This commission
was responsible for the delimitation of constituencies after the first Census
of independent India in 1951.
Second Delimitation Commission
: Set up in 1963 to
re-evaluate and adjust the boundaries of constituencies following the 1961
Census.
Third Delimitation Commission
: Constituted in 1973
after the 1971 Census, it was tasked with reassessing and redrawing
constituency boundaries.
Fourth Delimitation Commission
: Established in 2002,
based on the 2001 Census. This commission was significant as its
recommendations were implemented in 2008 and resulted in considerable changes
in the representation of various states in Lok Sabha and state assemblies. The
recommendations of this commission are applied to the electoral map used in
subsequent general elections.
Each of these commissions was tasked with ensuring the
constitutional requirement that the distribution of constituencies must be fair
and based primarily on the latest Census data, ensuring that each vote has
approximately equal weight irrespective of where it is cast.

Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
Konkani
Manipuri
Nepali
Maithili

: A language predominantly

Act, 2003. This amendment (71st Amendment) reflects India's policy of promoting
linguistic diversity and ensuring representation for major languages spoken by
various communities across the country.

Powers of the

answer "1, 2 and 3".

Inter-State trade and commerce is a State subject under the

This statement is incorrect. Corporation tax is a Union subject
under the Union List (Entry 85). It is collected by the central government and
not by the states.
Thus, the correct answer is
c)

the constitutional allocation of legislative powers related to Inter-State
quarantine.

Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of
India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy?
questions.solution_text:
The Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under the
Constitution of India, recognized and articulated by the Supreme Court in
several landmark judgments. Here is a breakdown of why the answer is Article
21:
Article 21
states: "No person shall be deprived
of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by
law." Over the years, the Supreme Court has interpreted "life"
and "personal liberty" in Article 21 to include various rights that
are essential for the enjoyment of a dignified human existence. The Right to
Privacy is one such right. In the landmark case of Justice K.S. Puttaswamy
(Retd.) vs Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court unequivocally held that the
Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and
personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.
The other articles mentioned have different implications:
Article 15
prohibits discrimination on grounds of
religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Article 16
provides for equality of opportunity in
matters of public employment.
Article 19
guarantees the six freedoms concerning
various rights, including speech and expression, assembly, association,
movement, residence, and profession.
Thus, the correct answer is
d) Article 21
, as it is the
constitutional provision under which the Right to Privacy is safeguarded.

What are the duties of the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) as
Head of the Department of Military Affairs?
Permanent
     Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee.
Exercise
     military command over the three Service Chiefs.
Principal
     Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on all triservice matters.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text:
The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) holds a critical and
influential role within the Indian Armed Forces as the head of the Department
of Military Affairs. Here's a breakdown of the duties that relate to the
options given:
Permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee.
This statement is correct. One of the primary roles of the CDS is
to serve as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee. In this
capacity, the CDS facilitates coordination, tri-service integration, and
ensures the implementation of combined strategies among the Indian Armed
Forces.
Exercise military command over the three Service Chiefs.
This statement is incorrect. The CDS does not exercise military
command over the Service Chiefs of the Army, Navy, and Air Force. Each of the
Service Chiefs retains operational control over their respective forces. The
CDS acts as a principal advisor and coordinates matters of tri-service
agencies, organizations, and commands, as well as integration and
prioritization of procurements.
Principal Military Advisor to the Defence Minister on all
triservice matters.
This statement is correct. The CDS acts as the principal military
advisor to the Defence Minister specifically on all tri-service matters. While
the respective Service Chiefs continue to advise the Minister on matters
specific to their respective services, the CDS focuses on combined concerns and
tri-service integration.
Therefore, the correct statements that describe the duties of the
CDS as the head of the Department of Military Affairs are 1 and 3, making the
correct answer
d) 1 and 3 only
.

: This operation was primarily

Operation Madad
: Often used for disaster relief
operations by the Indian Navy.

operations for the upliftment of local populations in remote areas is
c)
Operation Sadbhavana
.

questions.question_text:
The longest border between any two countries in the world is
between:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Canada and the United States of America

questions.solution_text:
The longest international land border between any two
countries in the world is indeed between Canada and the United States. This
border extends for approximately 8,891 kilometers (5,525 miles), running across
the North American continent from the Atlantic Ocean in the east to the Pacific
Ocean in the west. The border includes various terrains, crossing through
forests, mountains, plains, and water bodies, and it is marked in many places
by a clear cut known as the "border vista," a swath of land cleared
of all natural vegetation.
Here is a brief look at the borders of the other country pairs
mentioned:
Chile and Argentina
: This border is also one of
the longest in the world, stretching for about 6,691 kilometers (4,158 miles),
but it is shorter than the Canada-U.S. border.
China and India
: The border between these two
countries, known as the Line of Actual Control, is complex and contested but
measures around 3,488 kilometers (2,167 miles).
Kazakhstan and Russian Federation
: This
is one of the longer borders globally, spanning about 7,644 kilometers (4,750
miles), making it the second-longest continuous international border after the
Canada-U.S. border.
Therefore, the correct answer is
a) Canada and the United
States of America
, which have the longest shared border between any two
countries in the world.

meaning of constitutional articles to reflect contemporary realities or correct
interpretations.

: This entails the removal of existing provisions from the

methods—addition, variation, and repeal—to amend the Constitution. Therefore,
the correct answer is
d) 1, 2 and 3

Court or High Courts to :

options.label: A
options.option_text:
a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular
action.

options.label: B
options.option_text:
the Parliament/ Legislative Assembly to pass a law on

options.label: C
options.option_text:
the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a
case.

options.label: D
options.option_text:
the Government prohibiting it from following an
unconstitutional policy.

questions.solution_text:
A Writ of Prohibition is a constitutional remedy available
under Article 226 and Article 32 of the Constitution of India, primarily issued
by the High Courts and the Supreme Court. Here's a closer look at the purpose
and use of this writ:
Writ of Prohibition
: This writ is issued by a
higher court (like the Supreme Court or a High Court) to a lower court or a
tribunal to prevent the lower judicial authority from exceeding its
jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction with which it is not legally vested.
Essentially, the writ is meant to command the lower court to stop proceedings
in a particular case that is outside the bounds of its jurisdiction.
Here are the reasons why the other options are incorrect:
Option a
: A writ of prohibition is not generally directed towards
government officers to prevent them from taking particular actions; that would
more likely fall under a writ of mandamus or certiorari.
Option b
: This writ does not involve directing the Parliament or a
Legislative Assembly to pass legislation on prohibition or any other matter.
Legislative processes are outside the scope of judicial writs.
Option d
: While the writ of prohibition is aimed at preventing actions
outside of legal authority, it specifically targets judicial or quasi-judicial
bodies rather than the government's policy decisions. For unconstitutional
policies, other judicial reviews or writs like certiorari might be used.
Therefore, the correct answer is
c)
, focusing on the
prohibition against lower courts continuing proceedings in cases where they do
not possess jurisdiction.

Statement-II : The USA Government debt is not backed by any hard assets, but only by the faith of the Government.

options.label: A

questions.solution_text:
Statement-I
is correct. In the event of a default, the U.S. government would fail to meet its obligations to bondholders, meaning those holding Treasury bonds could not claim their expected payments. A default would imply the government's inability to fulfill its financial commitments as scheduled.
Statement-II
is also correct. U.S. government debt, like that of many other sovereign nations, is not backed by physical assets but rather by the "full faith and credit" of the government. This means that the government's ability to tax and to issue more debt is what underpins the debt, rather than specific collateral like gold or other assets.
While both statements are correct, Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. Statement-II provides a context about the nature of the debt being based on trust rather than tangible assets, which is foundational knowledge. However, Statement-I specifically addresses the implications of a default, which is a distinct issue from the basis of the debt's value. The cause of a default would not be simply because the debt is unbacked by hard assets, but rather due to a failure in the government's financial management or a severe fiscal crisis.

Consider the following statements in respect of the digital
rupee:
It is a
     sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment
     with its monetary policy.
It appears as
     a liability on the RBI’s balance sheet.
It is insured
     against inflation by its very design.
It is freely
     convertible against commercial bank money and cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.solution_text:
Statement 1
is correct. The digital rupee, or Central
Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), is indeed a sovereign currency issued by the
Reserve Bank of India. It is designed to complement the existing forms of money
and is aligned with the RBI's broader monetary policy objectives.
Statement 2
is also correct. Similar to physical
currency, the digital rupee would appear as a liability on the balance sheet of
the RBI. This is because it represents a claim against the central bank by the
holder of the digital currency.
Statement 3 incorrect.
The digital rupee, like any
currency, is not inherently insured against inflation. Its value would be
subject to the same economic forces that affect the value of physical currency,
including inflationary pressures. The statement that it is insured against
inflation by design is not accurate as no currency can inherently protect
against the loss of purchasing power due to inflation.
Statement 4
is correct. The digital rupee is intended
to be freely convertible against other forms of money, including commercial
bank deposits and cash. This convertibility is crucial for its functionality as
a medium of exchange, allowing users to seamlessly transact and convert between
digital and traditional forms of money.

. The

was introduced primarily in

by British
officials like
Thomas Munro

b) 2 only
.

With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the
following statements:
A bill
     pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution.
A bill passed
     by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution
     of the Lok Sabha.
A bill in
     regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to
     summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok
     Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.solution_text:
Statement 1 is Correct.
As per Article 107(5) of the
Indian Constitution, any bill that is still under consideration in the Lok
Sabha (i.e., not passed) lapses when the Lok Sabha is dissolved. This means the
bill has to be reintroduced in the newly elected House.
Statement 2 is Correct.
If a bill has been passed by
the Lok Sabha but is still pending in the Rajya Sabha at the time of
dissolution of the Lok Sabha, it also lapses. However, the new Lok Sabha can
introduce and pass it again.
Statement 3 is Incorrect.
If the President has already
notified a joint sitting under Article 108 to resolve a deadlock, the bill does
not lapse even if the Lok Sabha is dissolved. This provision ensures that an
important bill under dispute can still be passed despite Lok Sabha’s
dissolution.
Thus, statements 1 and 2 are correct. The correct answer is
(b)
1 and 2.

session.
Statement 3 is Correct.
The President dissolves the Lok
Sabha
on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
However, in exceptional
cases (such as when no party has a majority and a government cannot be formed),
the President may dissolve the Lok Sabha at their discretion.

.

.

birds,
bats, and insects
.

biofuels
through various methods
like
gasification
or
hydroprocessing
.

—can be used as feedstock

.
